article_lead.description: a central value of the posterior distribution used when absolute errors in a parameter estimate matter

new_bank_questions.title: A nonunique posterior median
new_bank_questions.body: A posterior puts probability 0.5 on θ=1 and 0.5 on θ=5. Which actions minimize posterior expected absolute error, and which action minimizes squared error? Give both risks at action 2.
new_bank_questions.answer: Every action in [1,5] is a posterior median and has absolute-error risk 0.5|a-1|+0.5|a-5|=2, including a=2. The posterior mean 3 uniquely minimizes squared error. At a=2 the squared-error risk is 0.5(1²)+0.5(3²)=5.

new_bank_questions.title: Transforming a posterior median
new_bank_questions.body: A probability θ has a posterior median 0.25. What is the posterior median of its odds θ/(1-θ)? Explain whether the odds of the posterior mean must equal the posterior mean of the odds.
new_bank_questions.answer: Odds are a strictly increasing function of θ, so their median is 0.25/(1-0.25)=1/3. Means do not generally commute with nonlinear transformations: E[θ/(1-θ)|x] need not equal E[θ|x]/(1-E[θ|x]), and the former may not even exist for some posteriors.
